Subject: Request for decision: scope & staffing for private hosting pilot (Acme Financial)

Team —

Acme is asking for a pilot to host their production workloads in a customer-managed VPC (optionally air-gapped). Before we commit, I need a quick decision on scope and required headcount. High-level asks below — please reply with short answers by EOD Thu 6/16.

1) Scope: VPC-only vs fully on-prem (what's the minimal acceptable scope for us to guarantee 99th %ile latency SLA?)
2) Security gates: SOC2 + network egress controls + KMS integration — any blockers we should flag now?
3) Resourcing: estimate minimum dedicated FTEs for infra (sustaining + oncall), SRE, and product support for a 3-month pilot.
4) Timeline & cost buckets: minimal calendar weeks to stand up, and quick order-of-magnitude monthly infra run-rate (gpus + networking + support).

Attached: design_request_v1.pdf (high-level pilot checklist)

If helpful, I can host a 30m sync tomorrow. Thanks — we need this packaged for an internal RFD to send to Sales/Legal.

— Lauren

Subject: Re: Request for decision: scope & staffing for private hosting pilot (Acme Financial)

Quick answers inline:

1) Scope: VPC-only covers 90% of use cases; fully on-prem (air-gapped) adds ~4-6 weeks of infra work (networking + supply chain). For initial SLA targets, VPC with dedicated hardware is fine.
2) Security gates: KMS/HSM integration is straightforward; the real unknown is outbound update channel for model weights in air-gapped setups — that'll need an explicit process.
3) Resourcing: min 1 infra eng (provisioning + network), 1 SRE (oncall & runbooks), 0.5 infra-systems (storage/backup). For on-prem add 1 field eng for procurement/installation.
4) Timeline/cost: VPC pilot 3–4 weeks; on-prem 8–10. Monthly infra run-rate (for a small GPU cluster): $25k–$45k depending on spot vs reserved and storage tier.

Link to infra runbook: https://drive.redwood.com/pri-hosting/infra-runbook (note: internal draft)

- Dev

Product considerations:
- Feature parity: We need to confirm which APIs (streaming, tool-calls, embeddings) must be supported in pilot. If Acme expects streaming + tool calling, we'll need to allocate QA cycles.
- Rollouts: can we support model pinning and automated fallback for pilot? If not, we should set that expectation.
- Acceptance criteria: (a) latency under 200ms median for short prompts, (b) successful end-to-end test with their sample traffic, (c) documented rollback.

Estimate: Product QA + docs 1.0 FTE for the pilot duration (0.75 if shared across pilots).

I'll compile an acceptance checklist and drop in the Drive link by Mon.
